title: Communicable Disease
before:
Measles Updates (May 2026)

The Maine CDC is connecting with partners to ensure communities, including schools, are prepared to identify, respond to, and prevent measles.

Maine CDC Update for Superintendents: Recording
Maine CDC Update for Superintendents: Slides
Federal CDC: Be Ready for Measles Toolkit
Maine CDC: Measles Resources

Communicable Disease Management

Schools should have protocols and procedures for:

  • Educating school personnel regarding symptoms and management of communicable diseases
  • Training for handling blood-borne pathogens (required by OSHA)
  • Keeping children with signs of communicable disease at home and seeking appropriate treatment
  • Record-keeping regarding non-immunized children during outbreaks
  • Exclusion and follow-up of children who are not immunized against vaccine-preventable diseases or who have contracted a communicable disease
  • Designating the school nurse (or other school official) as liaison with public health officials for the reporting of notifiable diseases and conditions
Resources
  • Communicable Disease Quick Guide
  • Maine CDC Communicable Disease School Health Resource
  • Checklist for Suspected Outbreak
Outbreak Reporting

A potential outbreak of disease is reportable to Maine CDC. In schools, this is defined as 15% of the school population being absent on a particular day due to illness. Schools must report elevated absenteeism. Using the NEO reporting tool will communicate with the Maine DOE and the Maine CDC.

  • 15% NEO Reporting Reference Guide
  • Maine CDC: 15% Absenteeism Guidance

Most diseases, such as ringworm, impetigo, and scabies, must be handled locally and not reported to public health officials. The Maine CDC School Health page contains disease-specific information sheets that include symptoms, causes, diagnosis, treatment, and role of the school nurse. Questions and consults may be addressed to disease.reporting@maine.gov or 1-800-821-5821.

Contact

Emily Poland, MPH, RN, NCSN
School Nurse Consultant
Email: Emily.Poland@maine.gov

decisions.label: Write the email addresses the same way
decisions.why: 1 address is shown in whatever case it was typed in. The house form capitalises each name and leaves a middle initial in lower case — disease.reporting@maine.gov → Disease.Reporting@maine.gov. Only the first letter of each part changes, so a name that spells itself LaBreck keeps doing so.

decisions.label: Let very uneven cards find their own height
decisions.why: 1 row pairs a short card with one holding nearly three times as much. Equal heights stretch the short one and the difference reads as a hole, so these are allowed to sit at the height of what is in them.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 2 rows hold two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 3× — 383 characters beside 129. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Make a loose address look like an address
decisions.why: 1 email address sits in the body of this page rather than in a contact block, drawn exactly like every other link — so the one that opens a mail window looks the same as the ones that go to web pages. The chip carries the same envelope the banner's contact link uses. The address itself does not change.

decisions.label: Remove the first section header
decisions.why: "Communicable Disease Management" repeats the page title, so the reader is told the same thing twice before any content.

decisions.label: Retire the old banner graphic
decisions.why: It repeats the page title in picture form, which the new banner already does in type.
